MAJOR: `_validate_cfg` findings are now appended instead of short-circuiting, so `_date_problems(item, cfg)` executes against a config already known to be malformed (e.g. `enforce_items` as an int/string). Iterating or `in`-testing that value can raise TypeError or emit substring false-positives, turning a gate report into a crash or noise — the exact fail-closed class this guard targets.

The three new config-shape branches (`enforce_items`, `required_sections`, `required_contracts`) have no test coverage; the only test change is a temp-filename tweak. Regressions in the new guard pass silently.
MINOR: `evaluate(item_id, item=None)` lets any caller supply an item without verifying `item.get("id") == item_id`, so a mismatched dict silently drives Gate 1 verdicts for a different id — integrity now depends on caller discipline rather than the gate.

`_validate_cfg` still reports only the first config defect (`return` on first failure), so operators iterating config repair see one error per run despite the "combined diagnostics" intent applied to config+date.
NIT: `main()` still fetches the item with `or {}`; an empty dict is passed into `evaluate`, which then hits the `if not item` path and reports "item not found" — correct outcome, but the sentinel obscures the intent for maintainers.
SUMMARY: The prior snapshot/diagnostic findings are addressed, but the fix now runs item date checks on a known-bad config (crash/false-positive risk) and ships three untested validation branches.
Top risks: gate robustness against malformed config, and unverified `evaluate(item=...)` input identity.
